gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 directly identifies that the defined self-normalized indicator approaches one for any nonzero update, so the advertised near-zero blending and smooth-region shut-off do not follow. It also distinguishes the unnormalized variant that alone has the claimed O(h^p) behavior, matching the gold defect and its specific correction.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the failure of the defined update-normalized indicator to produce small activation in generic smooth nonzero-update regions, and therefore the failure of the associated reduced-dissipation and scaling claims for the implemented method.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stated near-zero blending in smooth or near-steady regions is false for the defined self-normalized indicator: nonzero smooth updates can yield eta near one and s near one rather than shut-off.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that eta and s are approximately one whenever a smooth-region update is nonzero, so UM-SRD coincides with full SRD rather than removing dissipation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed smooth-update O(h^p) scaling and higher-order behavior apply only to an unnormalized indicator, not to the defined implementation.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the scaling and higher-order LTE result hold only for an explicitly unnormalized variant and proposes attributing the claim only to that variant.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 directly shows that under the full-mesh CFL the small-cell update retains a destabilizing contribution with weight 1-s, and that for arbitrarily small alpha the resulting coefficient can cause growth. This is the same failed inference that large updates necessarily restore enough SRD to yield uniform stability.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify that the blend does not become a uniformly stabilizing full-SRD update as the cut-cell volume tends to zero: a nonzero residual base-update component remains and can grow under the full-mesh timestep.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claim that a large unstable update necessarily re-engages sufficient SRD is false: as alpha tends to zero, activation need not eliminate the residual identity/base-update weight.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction computes the small-cell update and states that the blend retains it with weight 1-s, including a fixed activation value rather than becoming fully stabilizing as the cell shrinks.

component_coverage.gold_component: The residual destabilizing contribution can make the method non-TVD and unstable for arbitrarily small alpha under the stated full-mesh CFL, so near-full activation does not prove uniform stability.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the coefficient condition under which TV and maximum norm grow and explicitly rejects the claimed arbitrarily-small-cut-cell TVD/stability guarantee.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 diagnoses saturation of the normalized indicator for nonzero updates and the resulting failure of smooth-region shut-off. It does not recognize the distinct parameter-sensitivity defect that changing epsilon at updates comparable to epsilon changes eta and therefore s, nor the resulting invalid claim that epsilon needs no tuning.
